title: Politicians elected in the October 29th 2000 regional and municipal elections take office.
text: To ensure that all Wikipedia content is verifiable, Wikipedia provides a means for anyone to question an uncited claim. If your work has been tagged, please provide a reliable source for the statement, and discuss if needed.

title: The Colombian Government asks the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) to clarify whether they were responsible for the 29 December 2000 assassination of Congressperson Diego Turbay and his family in Caquetá.
text: Caquetá Department is one of the 32 departments of Colombia. It is located within the country's Amazon natural region and the Amazon rainforest.

title: 8-9 February – The FARC return to peace talks after meetings between Manuel "Sureshot" Marulanda and President Andrés Pastrana Arango.
text: Pedro Antonio Marín Marín, known by his "nom de guerre" Manuel Marulanda Vélez, was a Colombian militant who was the founder and main leader of the Marxist–Leninist FARC-EP ("Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia – Ejército del Pueblo"). Marulanda was born in a coffee-growing region of west-central Colombia in the Quindío Department, to a peasant family politically aligned with the Liberal Party during confl…

title: 24-27 February – President Pastrana meets with U.S. President George W. Bush in New York at the United Nations General Assembly.
text: George Walker Bush is an American retired politician and businessman who served as the 43rd president of the United States from 2001 to 2009. A member of the Republican Party, he previously served as the 46th governor of Texas from 1995 to 2000.

title: President Andrés Pastrana meets with Venezuelan president Hugo Chavez.
text: Andrés Pastrana Arango is a Colombian politician who was President of Colombia from 1998 to 2002, following in the footsteps of his father, Misael Pastrana Borrero, who was president from 1970 to 1974.

title: 10-13 April – Naya Massacre: Members of the Calima Front of the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC) kill around 50 mostly displaced Indigenous and Afro-Colombian people in Alto Naya, Cauca.
text: The United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia was a Far Right coalition of Colombian paramilitary organizations and vigilance committees that conceived itself as countering communist terrorism, banditry, and insurgency in Colombia. The AUC was an active belligerent in the Colombian conflict from 1997 to 2006.

title: A car bomb goes off in Parque Lleras in Medellín, killing at least seven people and injuring at least 50.
text: A car bomb, bus bomb, van bomb, lorry bomb, or truck bomb, also known as a vehicle-borne improvised explosive device, is an improvised explosive device designed to be detonated in an automobile or other vehicles. Car bombs can be roughly divided into two main categories: those used primarily to kill the occupants of the vehicle (often as an assassination) and those used as a means to kill, injure or damage people …

title: Uncertain date – The programadora En Vivo (previously Nuevos Días TV) ceases operations.
text: In Colombian broadcasting, programadoras are companies that produce television programs, especially for the public-commercial Canal Uno (and, until 2003, Canal A/Segunda Cadena). The Colombian television model from 1954 to the late 1990s, known as the sistema mixto ("mixed system"), relied on programadoras as the sole producers of programs that aired on the two major channels.

title: The 51st Vuelta a Colombia begins Ciudad de Popayán, Cauca.
text: Cauca Department is a department of Southwestern Colombia. Located in the southwestern part of the country, facing the Pacific Ocean to the west, the Valle del Cauca Department to the north, Tolima Department to the northeast, Huila Department to the east, and Nariño Department to the south.

title: The FARC-EP attack and break into La Picota prison in Bogotá with dynamite and the goal of breaking out FARC prisoners after the government refused to participate in a prisoners exchange. More than 140 prisoners fled, five were killed, and…
text: Dynamite is an explosive made of nitroglycerin, sorbents, and stabilizers. It was invented by Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel in 1866 and patented the following year.

title: 11–29 July – The 2001 Copa América is held in Colombia. At the finals in Bogotá on the 29th, Colombia wins 1–0 against México and Honduras wins third place against Uruguay after a penalty round.
text: The 2001 Copa América was held in Colombia, from 11 to 29 July. It was organised by CONMEBOL, South America's football governing body.

title: Bigamy ceases to be a criminal offense in Colombia.
text: In a culture where only monogamous relationships are legally recognized, bigamy is the act of entering into a marriage with one person while still legally married to another. A legal or de facto separation of the couple does not alter their marital status as married persons.

title: President Pastrana announces that he will be cutting off talks with the ELN in a speech to army personnel.
text: The Camilista Union - National Liberation Army, also known as the National Liberation Army - Camilista Union (Ejército de Liberación Nacional - Unión Camilista, ELN-UC), and originally called the National Liberation Army (ELN), is a Colombian far-left guerrilla organization involved in the continuing Colombian conflict since 1964. The ELN advocates a composite Catholic communist ideology of Marxism–Leninism, Camil…

title: Consuelo Araújo and 20 others are kidnapped by the 59th front of the FARC-EP in Patillal, Valledupar, Cesar.
text: Patillal is a populated center of Colombia and corregimiento in the municipality of Valledupar within the Colombian Department of Cesar. The town lies on the steps of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta with a semi-arid terrain.

title: Consuelo Araújo is killed during combat between the FARC-EP kidnappers and the National Army in La Mina, Valledupar, Cesar.
text: The National Army of Colombia is the land warfare service branch of the Military Forces of Colombia. With over 361,420 active personnel as of 2020, it is the largest and oldest service branch in Colombia, and is the second largest army in the Americas after the United States and before Brazil.

title: The Virgilio Barco Public Library in Bogotá opens.
text: Virgilio Barco Public Library is a Public library in the western sector of Bogotá, Colombia. It is a part of BibloRed, the District's Public Library Network.

title: En Colombia, paramilitares de las Autodefensas Unidas de Colombia (AUC), perpetuan la masacre de Chengue.
text: Las Autodefensas Unidas de Colombia​ fueron una organización paramilitar, narcotraficante, terrorista y contrainsurgente de extrema derecha que participó en el conflicto armado interno en Colombia entre 1997 hasta su desmovilización en 2006, con antecedentes de grupos paramilitares y dejando posteriores grupos disidentes y neoparamilitares.​ Se consolidó como agrupación de varios grupos paramilitares el 18 de abri…

title: el presidente Colombia, Andrés Pastrana se reuniría con el embajador británico Richard Ralph, con quien intentó negociar y hablar los problemas que enfrentaba Colombia contra el narcotráfico
text: Andrés Pastrana Arango es un abogado, periodista, empresario, y diplomático colombiano. Fue presidente de Colombia entre el 7 de agosto de 1998 y el 7 de agosto de 2002.​ Fue miembro del Partido Conservador Colombiano, es fundador y líder del movimiento Nueva Fuerza Democrática.

title: comienza la 40.ª edición de la Copa América 2001 por primera vez en Colombia como sede, a pesar de las amenazas de las FARC (Fuerzas Armadas Revolucionarias de Colombia) y de los Paramilitares para desestabilizar la realización del evento…
text: La Copa América 2001 fue la XL edición de la Copa América de fútbol. Esta versión del torneo se realizó en Colombia, entre el 11 y 29 de julio de 2001, y supuso la primera vez de dicho país como anfitrión oficial (anteriormente en Colombia se habían jugado algunos partidos de las ediciones 1975, 1979 y 1983; debido a que en esos años la Copa América se disputaba sin sede fija —se jugó en todos los países afiliados…

title: en Bogotá (Colombia) finaliza la Copa América 2001, donde la selección de Colombia se consagra campeón y obtiene su primer título de Copa América tras vencer por la mínima diferencia de un gol por cero a la selección de México con gol de…
text: La Copa América —oficialmente, Conmebol Copa América— es el principal torneo internacional oficial de fútbol masculino en América del Sur. Inicialmente denominada Campeonato Sudamericano de Selecciones, Campeonato Sudamericano de Fútbol o simplemente Campeonato Sudamericano, adquirió su nombre actual en 1975.

title: en la carretera que conduce de Sogamoso a Yopal (Colombia), un grupo de paramilitares detiene un bus con 18 pasajeros, separan a dos niños y una anciana y fusilan a los otros 15 hombres y mujeres y el cierre de Trans World Airlines Twa.
text: Trans World Airlines, conocida comúnmente como TWA, fue una importante aerolínea estadounidense. Fue fundada en 1925 bajo el nombre de Western Air Express y en 1930​ pasó a denominarse Trans World Airlines, hasta que en 2001 fue comprada por American Airlines.

title: Fútbol Profesional Colombiano: América de Cali, campeón.
text: La División Mayor del Fútbol Colombiano es una entidad deportiva que forma parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y se encarga de organizar, administrar y reglamentar los torneos de fútbol profesional en Colombia: Primera A; Primera B; la Copa Colombia, la Superliga de Colombia y la Liga Femenina.

title: Los niños invisibles
text: Los niños invisibles es una película dramática colombiana de 2001 dirigida y escrita por Lisandro Duque Naranjo​ y protagonizada por Guillermo Castañeda, Ingrid Cielo Ospina, Gustavo Camacho, Gustavo Angarita y Marcela Valencia.

title: La pena máxima
text: La pena máxima es una película colombiana escrita por Luis Felipe Salamanca y Darío García sobre un cuento homónimo de José Luis Varela. Fue dirigida por Jorge Echeverry, estrenada el 15 de junio de 2001 y protagonizada por Enrique Carriazo.​ Relata la historia de un hombre que tras una enorme obsesión con la selección colombiana cometerá la peor decisión de su vida.

title: Bogotá 2016
text: Bogotá 2016 es una película de ciencia ficción colombiana de 2001 dirigida por Alessandro Basile, Ricardo Guerra, Pablo Mora y Jaime Sánchez y protagonizada por Cristina Umaña, John Alex Toro, Jaime Barbini, Verónica Orozco, Valentina Gómez, Fernando Solórzano, César Mora, Mario Duarte y Diana Ángel. Está conformada por tres historias, "¿Quién paga el pato?", "La Venus virtual" y "Zapping".

title: The NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft lands in the "saddle" region of 433 Eros, becoming the first spacecraft to land on an asteroid.
text: Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous, later renamed NEAR Shoemaker in honor of planetary scientist Eugene Shoemaker, was a robotic space probe developed by the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory for NASA. Launched in 1996, it was designed to study the near-Earth asteroid 433 Eros from orbit over the course of a year. It was the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and successfully land on one.

title: NASA's Genesis spacecraft is launched.
text: Genesis was a NASA sample-return probe that collected a sample of solar wind particles and returned them to Earth for analysis. It was the first NASA sample-return mission to return material since the Apollo program, and the first to return material from beyond the orbit of the Moon.

title: NASA's Galileo spacecraft passes within 112 miles (180 km) of Jupiter's moon Io.
text: Galileo was an American robotic space probe that studied the planet Jupiter and its moons, as well as the asteroids Gaspra and Ida. Named after the Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei, it consisted of an orbiter and an entry probe.

title: The Hubble Space Telescope detects sodium in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b, the first exoplanet atmosphere to be measured.
text: The Hubble Space Telescope is a space telescope that was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 on STS-31 and remains in operation. It is regarded as one of the largest and most versatile space telescopes, renowned as a vital research tool and as a public relations boon for astronomy.

title: The author Michael Crichton signs a new deal with HarperCollins Publishers that reportedly earns him $40 million for two books.
text: John Michael Crichton was an American author and filmmaker. His books have sold over 200 million copies worldwide, and over a dozen have been adapted into films.

title: The BookCrossing scheme for leaving books for strangers to find is launched.
text: BookCrossing is defined as the practice of leaving a book in a public place to be 'caught' by others, who may then do likewise. The term is derived from bookcrossing.com, a free online book community which was founded in 2001 to encourage the practice, aiming to "make the whole world a library." The "crossing" or exchanging of books may take any of a number of forms, including the 'wild-release' of a book in publi…

title: The film version of Helen Fielding's 1996 novel Bridget Jones's Diary has uncredited cameo roles as themselves for Salman Rushdie, Julian Barnes and Jeffrey Archer, at a literary party.
text: Helen Fielding is a British journalist, novelist and screenwriter, best known as the creator of the fictional character Bridget Jones. Fielding’s first novel was set in a refugee camp in East Africa and she started writing Bridget Jones in an anonymous column in London’s Independent newspaper.

title: The English popular novelist and politician Jeffrey Archer, having been found guilty of perjury in a libel trial, is sentenced to imprisonment.
text: Jeffrey Howard Archer, Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare was an English novelist and politician. He served as Member of Parliament (MP) for Louth, Lincolnshire, from the 1969 by-election until 1974, when he did not seek re-election after almost going bankrupt.

title: Amiri Baraka reads his poem "Somebody Blew Up America?" at a poetry festival in New Jersey, eight days after the September 11 attacks.
text: Amiri Baraka, previously known as LeRoi Jones and Imamu Amear Baraka, was an American writer of poetry, drama, fiction, essays, and music criticism. He was the author of numerous books of poetry and taught at several universities, including the University at Buffalo and Stony Brook University.

title: Film premiere of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, first in the commercially successful Harry Potter film series based on the novels of J. K. Rowling.
text: Joanne Rowling, better known by her pen name J. K. Rowling, is a British author, philanthropist, producer and screenwriter. She is best known for writing Harry Potter, a seven-volume fantasy series about a young wizard and the best-selling book series in history, with over 600 million copies sold.

title: The live-action film version of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, directed by Peter Jackson, opens in London. Its appearance has a strong impact on readership of the trilogy.
text: John Ronald Reuel Tolkien was an English writer and academic philologist. He was the author of the high fantasy works The Hobbit (1937) and The Lord of the Rings (1954–1955).

title: A black monolith measuring approximately 9 feet tall appears in Seattle, Washington's Magnuson Park, placed by an anonymous artist in reference to the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey.
text: In Arthur C. Clarke's Space Odyssey series, Monoliths are machines in black cuboids whose sides extend in the precise ratio of 1 : 4 : 9 built by an unseen extraterrestrial species whom Clarke dubbed the Firstborn and who he suggests are the earliest highly intelligent species to evolve in the Milky Way. In the series of novels (and the films based on these), three Monoliths are discovered in the Solar System by a…

title: Unveiling of Rachel Whiteread's Untitled Monument on the Fourth plinth, Trafalgar Square, London.
text: Dame Rachel Whiteread is an English artist who primarily produces sculptures, which typically take the form of casts. She was the first woman to win the annual Turner Prize in 1993.

title: Inauguration of the Altamira cave replica created by Manuel Franquelo and Sven Nebel.
text: The Cave of Altamira is a cave complex, located near the historic town of Santillana del Mar in Cantabria, Spain. It is renowned for prehistoric cave art featuring charcoal drawings and polychrome paintings of contemporary local fauna and human hands.

title: An estimated $100 million worth of art is destroyed in the 11 September attacks on New York City. Public artwork accounts for around $10 million of this figure, which includes works by Alexander Calder, Joan Miró and Roy Lichtenstein.
text: The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001. A total of 19 hijackers commandeered four commercial passenger airliners.

title: Fritz Koenig's Great Spherical Caryatid ("The Sphere") is the only surviving artwork following the September 11 attacks. It is repurposed as a memorial.
text: Fritz Koenig was a German sculptor, considered one of the most important international German sculptors of the 20th century. Koenig's main work and most famous work is The Sphere.
